title: Massed bands at Booker T. Washington Auditorium and tuba duel
summary: At Sunday school parades five bands played together on the steps, and two tuba players including Wilbert Tillman traded phrases.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: I remember now that you were talking about multiple bands that there were a couple of occasions when, for Sunday school parades, when they got to the Booker T. Washington Auditorium and the marches in the parade had to walk up these long steps to get into the big double doors, that the first band in the parade would pull off and stand at the foot of the steps and play, and as the other bands caught up, they would have this masked band effect, and by the time the whole parade was in, there'd be, on one occasion, there were five bands that were there playing all together, playing when the Saints go marching in, and, you know, it would go on for a long time because it was a long parade, and it took a long time for everybody to get up the steps and inside the hall, and that was pretty exciting music. One occasion, I remember two of the bass horn players, tuba players, Wilbert Tillman was one of them, and I don't know who the other person was, but they were playing in this masked band thing, and they were standing just facing each other, practically bell to bell, and they were just having a wonderful time trying to blow each other off the street. And they would, one would play a little phrase, and the other would pick it up and blow it right back at them, and at the other one, they'd trade things back and forth, and when one would do a particularly hard sequence, or they liked the way it'd all come out, they'd stop and throw their heads back and just laugh like hell,
They were having a wonderful time trying to blow each other off the street, and it was quite a display.
